text:
Register entry for the construct '<DIRECTIVE>, this-once | <DIRECTIVE>, from-now-on'.
Meaning: A tag in fixed final position on a directive (an instruction, a request, or a stated preference). '<DIRECTIVE>, this-once' = 'do this for the item at hand only; this instruction does not govern later comparable work, and the receiver must not record it as a standing preference.' '<DIRECTIVE>, from-now-on' = 'do this for the item at hand and for all later comparable work, until the instruction is explicitly revoked; the receiver should record it as standing.' The tag types the directive's PERSISTENCE - how long the instruction lives - and nothing else. It does not change the directive's strength, urgency, or priority; it does not say whether failure is tolerated (that is attempt:/ensure:); it makes no claim about whether the CURRENT attempt may be retried; and it neither licenses nor forbids delegation (that is no-delegation / one-hop-delegation-allowed). 'Comparable work' means work of the same kind as the item at hand, not all work whatsoever. Bare directives remain legal and unmarked; the tag is used when persistence scope is load-bearing.
Slot: this-once = the directive governs the item at hand only; it does not govern later comparable work and must not be recorded as a standing preference; from-now-on = the directive governs the item at hand and all later comparable work until explicitly revoked; it should be recorded as standing
Example: Use British spelling, this-once. / Run the linter before you commit, from-now-on.
In careful English: Use British spelling for this document only — do not carry it into my later work and do not save it as a preference. / Run the linter before you commit, and keep doing so on every future commit until I say otherwise.
